Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The players are already out in the middle now. Alick Athanaze and Jewel Andrew are the two openers for West Indies. Shaheen Afridi to start proceedings with the ball. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then! A must win game for West Indies and they have done half of the job. It should be an easy win for them but you never know which West Indies will step out. Can Pakistan make it difficult for them? Stay tuned to find out.

Jason Holder, the man of the moment, is up for a quick chat. He says that it swings upfront, so he used it to his advantage. Adds that he got a couple of new ball wickets, which helpe,d and Akeal Hosein helped from the other end as well. Mentions that he wasn't trying to challenge the conditions and tried to stick to his strengths. Says that it was good to contribute upfront as well as at the death, as he has been working hard to improve his skills. Further adds that it has been a tough few weeks for the team, but they got the chance to celebrate in this game, so they made the most of it. Ends by saying that he is hoping they can celebrate even more by chasing the total down.

Pakistan were struggling to get going and were looking for a big partnership. Salman Agha, the skipper, entered when Pakistan were under a lot of pressure. He played with intent and got able support from Hasan Nawaz at the other end. The duo added more than fifty, with Hasan Nawaz hitting Romario Shepherd for a hat-trick of sixes. It felt like the momentum was shifting but Pakistan lost both the set batters in the following overs and never recovered after that.

Interestingly, both teams wanted to bat first today but only one made it count. West Indies got rid of Saim Ayub inside the Powerplay, eventually keeping them reeling inside the first six overs with three wickets fallen. West Indies continued to bowl well, keeping it tight and executing the plans but the one thing they rectified from the first game was their fielding effort. The good bowling was backed by some top fielding. West Indies in recent matches have allowed teams to get back in the game and almost let loose of the pressure today as well but Shai Hope with his brilliant captaincy, made sure not to make the same mistakes and with the bowling changes today got it done according to the plans.

Excellent, excellent, excellent! Top, top stuff from West Indies as they have earned their strides in the first half of the game. Superb display of bowling led by Jason Holder, who ends with a four-fer but overall, the leading wicket taker for West Indies in T20Is.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for action. Two umpires make their way to the middle. West Indies follow them to their respective positions. Sahibzada Farhan and Saim Ayub to open for Pakistan. Akeal Hosein to bowl first...

The captain of West Indies, Shai Hope says they would have batted first as well. Admits the biggest threat is to play the spin in these conditions. Hopes to turn things around and keep the series alive. Informs Alick Athanaze and Keacy Carty come in for Johnson Charles and Jediah Blades.

Salman Agha, the skipper of Pakistan says they will bat first as it looks like a slow surface and they want to try a couple of things before the Asia Cup. Informs Hasan Ali comes in for Haris Rauf, who has been rested.

TOSS - Pakistan have won the toss and will BAT.

West Indies are winless in six T20Is in a row, losing all five against Australia and then the first game. They have the power and the big name but they are missing a collective performance. Once again, their batting prowess was under scrutiny. The openers struggled to get going and once they got out, there was too much of a task left to do for the remaining batters. Credit to Pakistani bowlers. They kept it simple and got the reward. Can they repeat a similar performance and seal the series, or will West Indies bounce back? Toss and team sheets next.

Hello everyone to the second T20I between Pakistan and West Indies. The series have settled to 1-0 with Pakistan taking the points and looking to wrap up the series today. Pakistan were competitive and brilliant in all three-departments of the game. Saim Ayub stepped up with the bat and there were a couple of cameos from the middle order as well to take the total above 175. During the chase, Pakistan were ruthless and kept it tight throughout. Ayub turned up with the ball, scalping two wickets, eventually bagging all the awards as well. Pakistan will hope for a similar performance and win the series.
...MATCH DAY...

The second T20I of the three-match series between West Indies and Pakistan comes calling at the Central Broward Park and Broward County Stadium in Lauderhill. Pakistan have drawn first blood in the series and will be keen to wrap it up, while West Indies, who have now lost six T20Is in a row, will be eager to bounce back and keep the series alive. Chasing a manageable target of 179 in the first T20I, the West Indies made a steady start through their openers but struggled to accelerate during the middle overs. That left too much for those that followed, and Pakistan's spinners capitalised by picking up wickets at regular intervals. With Brandon King, Rovman Powell and Shimron Hetmyer unavailable, the responsibility falls on Shai Hope, Johnson Charles and Sherfane Rutherford. Hope, the highest run-scorer for the hosts in their recent series against Australia, will once again be a key figure. There were a few positives with the ball for the West Indies, particularly a three-wicket haul from Shamar Joseph on his return to the T20I side. However, Shai Hope might reflect on his bowling choices, having used only 7 overs of spin in helpful conditions and not turning to Gudakesh Motie at all. After a disappointing series loss in Bangladesh, Salman Agha and his team have made a strong start to this tour. Saim Ayub's 57 stood out in the first game, with useful contributions from others. Fakhar Zaman and Salman Agha have not had a significant impact in recent matches and will be keen to make a mark. With the ball, the combination of Mohammad Nawaz, Sufiyan Muqeem and Saim Ayub worked well to plug away at the wickets, but Haris Rauf and Faheem Ashraf were expensive and will look to bounce back with better discipline in this outing. Can the hosts deliver a complete performance across departments and take the series into a decider? Or will Pakistan hand West Indies yet another series defeat? We shall find out.
